sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 23.01.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Vikrant Neeraj, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Ms. Pallavi Rani, learned counsel holding brief of Shri Rajesh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the first informant and Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 17 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii). The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life. There is no lawful basis for the age related entry of the victim in the school records.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The school records disclosing her age as 17 years are unreliable.

(iii) The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 17 years of age while in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she stated that she is 17 years of age (iv) Medico-legal examination (not the age determination test) records that the victim is 17 years of age.

No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as it would establish the majority of the victim and falsify the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.
3. The victim and the applicant were intimate.
4. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship with the applicant.
5. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that she was enticed by the applicant into accompanying him to Meerut.

However, in the latter part of the said statement, false and aggravated allegations have been made against the applicant at the behest of her parents only to deflect attention from her own conduct and to save the failing prosecution case.

sentences.text: 6. The victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has asserted that she accompanied the applicant to Meerut to get married to him.
She has further stated that she stayed with the applicant in a rented accommodation of her own volition.

7. The victim has not made any allegation of commission of rape, abduction or forceful assault by the applicant in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
8.
The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places.
She did not raise an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
Her conduct shows that she was a consenting party.
9. Major inconsistencies in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C., as well as the recitals in the F.I.R. discredit the prosecution case.
10. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
11. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.

12. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
13.
The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Ankit be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the Ankit vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171441722/
